newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 29.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- SAFEWAY LINKS WITH ABBEY FOR CARDS LAUNCH

Safeway yesterday revealed plans to launch debit and credit cards and other financial products in partnership with Abbey National. The first bonus card, ABC Card, will be launched next Spring and will bear interest. It will be possible to use the card at some other stores.
-- BRITISH GAS LOSSES DEEPEN

British Gas yesterday revealed third-quarter losses on deals of 294 million pounds stg, the result of costly supply contracts with Europe. These costs, along with industrial market losses and customer service problems, resulted in a 346 million pound loss for the three months to the end of September.
-- OUTLOOK STORMY FOR INSURANCE FRAUDSTERS

The Meterological Office will next week launch a product making it easier for insurers to check the validity of weather damage claims. GeoProof will provide detailed weather data to subscribing insurance companies the following morning.
THE TIMES
-- A&L FACES LEGAL ACTION OVER PLANNED 2.5 BILLION POUNDS FLOAT

The Alliance & Leicester are facing legal action from members over the building society's planned stock flotation. The Alliance & Leicester Action Group are planning the legal action following the society's board meeting to discuss a proposed new building Societies Bill that could affect its plans to become a bank early next year.
-- P&O LINK-UP WITH STENA SENT TO MMC

The proposed merger of the cross-Channel ferry fleets of P&O and Stena was put into confusion yesterday when Ian Lang, the president of the Board of Trade, referred the deal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. The MMC investigation should be completed by March 6, but spoils the ferry company's plans to market the new venture to the travel industry over the winter.
-- RBS RECORD MARRED BY DIRECT LINE SETBACK

The Royal Bank of Scotland's telephone insurance subsidiary, Direct Line, reported pre-tax profits of 26 million pounds stg for the year to September 30, down from 86 million. The drop was attributed to severe winter weather and fierce competition in the motor insurance market. Direct Line insists it would start to make big profits again within two years, but that motor insurance might be eclipsed by income from household insurance and personal financial services.
THE GUARDIAN
-- BASS URGES DTI TO MAKE ITS MOVE ON CARLSBERG

Bass yesterday called on the DTI to make a quick decision on whether to refer its purchase of a half-share in Carlsberg-Tetley to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. The Office of Fair Trading has passed its recommendation on the deal to the department. Analysts said Bass may have to dispose of a large part of its tied pubs to avoid a lengthy inquiry.
-- DUREX MAKERS EYE US MARKET

London International Group, makers of Durex condoms, announced half-year profits up 46 percent to 9.5 million pounds before exceptional items. The group is thought likely to meet its target of 15 percent operating profit the following year. The group wants to boost its US profile, where it is currently No 2 in the market.
-- ENTENTE AT RISK OVER EMU RULES

A leading Bank of France adviser yesterday accused Germany of overriding France's economic interests. A debate on possible devaluation of the franc was called for. President Chirac and Chancellor Kohl are to meet tomorrow, and a more formal meeting before the Dublin summit in mid-December will follow.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- POWER FREE-FOR-ALL 'WILL COST 1 BILLION POUNDS'

A senior executive warned yesterday that the opening of the electricity market to full competition in 1998 will cost near to 50 pounds stg for every domestic customer in the land, or 1 billion pounds stg. Brian Staple, chief executive of United Utilities, said that the costs were so great they could not be borne by the electricity companies alone and would have to be passed on to the UK's 22 million consumers.
-- SOUTHERN ELECTRIC TO PAY OUT 180 MILLION POUNDS

The regional power company Southern Electric is to give bakc 180 million pounds stg to shareholders by the end of the financial year. The company has delayed the final decision on how to repay shareholders because the Chancellor last month outlawed tax credits on such payments. The company says its decision to hand back the cash is due to bills being 180 million pounds stg lower in real terms than they were six years ago.
-- UNITED AND HTV MAY SHARE SERVICES

United News & Media and HTV have started talks on closer co-operation, according to industry sources. On the agenda are transmission services, joint news gathering and coproduction. The talks follow United's purchase earlier this month of a 20 percent stake in HTV, the ITV licence holder for Wales and the West. Analysts expect that United could be interested in buying HTV outright once Takeover Panel rules allow it to do so.
